title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 178 (Nomination and Remuneration Committee and Stakeholders Relationship Committee)

content.overview: Section 178 requires every listed public company and such other class or classes of companies as may be prescribed to constitute a Nomination and Remuneration Committee of three or more non-executive directors, of which not less than one-half shall be independent directors. The committee formulates criteria for determining qualifications, positive attributes and independence of a director, identifies persons for appointment as directors and senior management, recommends a policy relating to remuneration, and specifies the manner for effective evaluation of performance. A company which consists of more than one thousand shareholders, debenture-holders, deposit-holders and any other security holders at any time during a financial year shall constitute a Stakeholders Relationship Committee to consider and resolve the grievances of security holders. The chairperson of the company may be appointed as a member of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee but shall not chair such Committee.
content.glance: Listed and prescribed companies: NRC of ≥3 non-executive directors, ≥½ independent; identifies candidates, sets evaluation and remuneration policy. >1000 security holders: Stakeholders Relationship Committee for grievances. Company chair may be NRC member but not chair.
content.study: The Board of Directors of every listed public company and such other class or classes of companies as may be prescribed shall constitute the Nomination and Remuneration Committee consisting of three or more non-executive directors out of which not less than one-half shall be independent directors. The Nomination and Remuneration Committee shall identify persons who are qualified to become directors and who may be appointed in senior management, recommend to the Board their appointment and removal, and shall specify the manner for effective evaluation of performance of Board, its committees and individual directors; formulate the criteria for determining qualifications, positive attributes and independence of a director and recommend to the Board a policy relating to the remuneration for the directors, key managerial personnel and other employees. The Stakeholders Relationship Committee shall consider and resolve the grievances of security holders of the company. The chairperson of the company may be appointed as a member of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee but shall not chair such Committee. Current-law framing: confirm company class; check NRC composition and functions; apply Stakeholders Committee threshold; note chair restriction.

sections.heading: NRC Constitution
sections.body: Listed public companies and prescribed classes must have an NRC of three or more non-executive directors, of which not less than one-half are independent.

sections.heading: NRC Functions
sections.body: Identify persons for directorship and senior management; recommend appointment and removal; specify performance evaluation manner; formulate criteria for qualifications, attributes and independence; recommend remuneration policy.

sections.heading: Stakeholders Relationship Committee
sections.body: Required where the company has more than one thousand shareholders, debenture-holders, deposit-holders and other security holders at any time in a financial year; resolves grievances of security holders.

sections.heading: Chair Restriction
sections.body: The chairperson of the company may be a member of the NRC but shall not chair it.

provisions.title: Nomination and Remuneration Committee and Stakeholders Relationship Committee

examples.title: NRC composition
examples.body: A listed company constitutes an NRC of four non-executive directors of whom two are independent. Section 178 requires not less than one-half independent, so the composition is compliant only if the independent count meets that floor.

examples.title: Stakeholders threshold
examples.body: A company has 1,200 security holders during the year. It must constitute a Stakeholders Relationship Committee under s. 178.

hypotheticals.question: May the company’s chairperson chair the NRC?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 178 expressly provides that the chairperson of the company may be appointed as a member of the NRC but shall not chair such Committee.

distinctions.title: NRC / Stakeholders (s. 178) vs Audit Committee (s. 177)
distinctions.left: Nomination, remuneration, evaluation and security-holder grievances
distinctions.right: Financial reporting, auditor independence, RPT approval and vigil mechanism

misconceptions.trap: Every company must have both an NRC and a Stakeholders Relationship Committee.
misconceptions.correction: NRC is required for listed public companies and prescribed classes. Stakeholders Relationship Committee is required only when security holders exceed one thousand at any time in the year.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 178 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm company class. II. Check NRC composition and functions. III. Apply Stakeholders threshold. IV. Note chair restriction. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Class facts; composition; functions; threshold; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 178 requires prescribed companies to constitute a Nomination and Remuneration Committee with a majority-independent non-executive composition and, where security holders exceed one thousand, a Stakeholders Relationship Committee.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Board processes for selecting and remunerating directors and for handling security-holder grievances are institutionalised through mandatory committees.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 178 is the people-and-grievances committee companion to the audit committee in s. 177.
